Confidence intervals for nbreg and zinbreg fits

Source: R/inference.R
confint-nbzinbreg.Rd

Confidence intervals for the coefficients and for the dispersion parameter theta.

  • Coefficients: Wald intervals, estimate plus or minus qnorm((1 + level) / 2) standard errors, as confint.default() gives for glm.nb and zeroinfl fits.

  • theta, method = "profile" (the default): the profile-likelihood interval, all values of theta whose profile log-likelihood (maximized over the coefficients with theta held fixed) lies within qchisq(level, 1) / 2 of the maximum. It is always positive and can be asymmetric.

  • theta, method = "wald": the Wald interval on the log scale, exp(log(theta) +- z SE(log theta)), which also stays positive.

For zinbreg fits the coefficients are named as by coef() (count_*, zero_*), followed by "theta".

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, method = c("profile", "wald"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbzinbreg_confint'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, method = c("profile", "wald"), ...)

Arguments

object

An nbreg or zinbreg fit.

parm

Which parameters to give intervals for: names (the coefficient names and "theta") or indices into them; all by default.

level

Confidence level, strictly between 0 and 1.

method

For theta: "profile" (profile likelihood, the default) or "wald". The coefficients always get Wald intervals.

...

Not used (an error if supplied), except for print().

x

A nbzinbreg_confint object, for print().

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

Value

A matrix of class nbzinbreg_confint with one row per parameter and columns for the lower and upper limits, labelled as in stats::confint(). Attributes: status (a matrix of the same shape: "wald", "finite", "unbounded", ...), method and level.

Details

How the profile interval is found. No root finder is used. The search works on log(theta): it steps outward from the estimate (first by max(0.1, SE(log theta)), then doubling the step) until the deviance 2 (loglik - profile loglik) exceeds the cutoff, then bisects between the last point inside and the first point outside until they are within 1e-6 on the log scale. At every trial value the coefficients are refitted with theta held fixed (warm-started, and retried from a fresh start if needed); a value is used only if that fit converged. For zinbreg each such fit is a full EM run with theta held fixed, which must also pass the gradient check over its free parameters, so a profile interval takes many EM fits (typically 30 to 60; a minute or more on data of a few thousand rows). method = "wald" is immediate.

Endpoints that are not ordinary numbers. The "status" attribute (and the printed notes) say what each endpoint is:

  • "unbounded": the upper limit is Inf. The profile reaches the search bound theta_max without crossing the cutoff, and the profile is certified to have reached its limit as theta grows: it no longer changes, for nbreg it equals the Poisson log-likelihood, and that limit lies inside the likelihood-ratio region at the requested level. The data are then consistent with no overdispersion at all.

  • "beyond theta_max" or "below theta_min": the limit lies outside the numerical bounds and could not be resolved; it is NA (with a warning), never silently set to the bound or to Inf.

  • "inner fit failed": a fit with theta held fixed did not converge; that limit is NA, with a warning.

  • "diverging", "no standard error", "theta on a bound": no Wald interval can be given; the limits are NA.

If any trial value gives a profile log-likelihood above the fitted maximum (by more than 1e-6 * (|loglik| + 1)), the fit is not at its maximum: the model is refitted from there to confirm it, and an error is raised instead of an interval around a point that is not the maximum.

Errors and warnings

  • nbzinbreg_error_input: object of the wrong class, an invalid parm (unknown names, out-of-range, non-finite or duplicated indices), level outside (0, 1), an invalid method, or unused arguments.

  • nbzinbreg_error_fit: the fit is not at its maximum (see above).

  • nbzinbreg_warning_convergence: an inner fit failed, or the profile is not unimodal.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_theta: a limit lies beyond theta_max or below theta_min and is NA.

See also

nbreg(), zinbreg(), tidy.nbreg()

Examples

d <- data.frame(x = 1:8, y = c(1, 0, 6, 1, 9, 2, 20, 4))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = d)
confint(fit)
#>                2.5 % 97.5 %
#> (Intercept) -1.76281 1.5361
#> x            0.04114 0.6468
#> theta        0.39916 6.3575
confint(fit, "theta", method = "wald")
#>        2.5 % 97.5 %
#> theta 0.3984  5.716
confint(fit, 1:2, level = 0.9)
#>                  5 %   95 %
#> (Intercept) -1.49762 1.2709
#> x            0.08983 0.5981
